xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2541: move pipeline state to same-repo orphan branch overdeck-state with a dedicated writer worktree

plan.title: feat(state-plane): move pipeline state to same-repo orphan branch overdeck-state with a dedicated writer worktree
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: The deacon and pipeline mirror the durable state plane (records, continues, specs, drafts, review/test/feedback artifacts, backlog, and the beads DB) into git by committing to the same branch and worktree as the code. That single design causes three incident classes seen on 2026-07-09 alone: (1) the PAN-2468 review-reset loop, where high-frequency state commits on main force constant feature-branch rebases that rewrite every SHA and make a passed review look like new code; (2) writer races where the deacon's chore(state) auto-commit in the primary worktree is silently absorbed by a concurrent human/agent git commit --amend; and (3) history and CI pollution, where git log main interleaves state noise, state pushes trigger CI, and code exists (pipeline-state-paths.ts, state-plane.ts) largely to discriminate state commits from code commits after the fact.
narratives.Proposal: Move the state plane off code branches onto a same-repo orphan branch named overdeck-state, written ONLY through a dedicated writer worktree at ${OVERDECK_HOME}/state/<projectKey>. The orphan branch's tree is flat (records/ continues/ specs/ drafts/ review/ test/ feedback/ backlog/ notes/ .beads/ at its root, no .pan/ wrapper); main gitignores those paths; CI guards fail either branch on a violation. Migration detection is repo-derived (the overdeck-state branch exists on origin), never machine-local config, so every clone resolves correctly with zero per-machine setup. Everything resolves through a new resolveStateHome() chokepoint that extends resolveInfraRepo(); read doors, the write door, and project-scope beads all resolve through it, with read-only legacy .pan/ fallback during migration. The context layer moves out of state entirely to .overdeck/context/ on main (code-owned, reviewable). Every behavior change is gated per project on isStateMigrated(), so unmigrated projects are untouched; overdeck dogfoods first via an idempotent pan admin state migrate command, and the multi-project rollout is the same one command per repo (plain git, works on GitLab too).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Renaming the pan CLI, the src/lib/pan-dir/ module, or issue prefixes (D7; PAN-1952 naming policy keeps prefixes).
- Removing the checkPostReviewCommits benign-move guards (D11 keeps them as backstops until telemetry shows they no longer fire).
- Extending multi-tenant / separate-repo state homes: the pan_records.repo polyrepo path keeps working as the documented escape hatch but is not extended here.
- Any bd-internal changes: the redirect retarget (D13) is a one-path-string change in Overdeck's own initializeWorkspaceBeads, not a beads modification.
- Remote (Fly) state sync for migrated projects: D14 blocks remote spawns on migrated projects; the redesign is a named follow-up issue, not part of this delivery.
- History rewrite on main: migration makes only ordinary, revertible commits (NFR-1).

autoDecisions.summary: Adopted every design decision D1-D14 from the PRD (.pan/drafts/pan-2541.md) as authoritative without re-litigating.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD was operator-directed and pre-decided branch name (overdeck-state), flat tree layout, no symlinks, repo-derived migration detection, redirect retarget, and the Fly D14 block. Auto-planning rule: when the issue/PRD documents the recommended option, choose it and record it rather than asking.

autoDecisions.summary: Split WI-7 into four beads (STATE_BRANCH_PATHS constant, CI guards, stray-write lint, recreation tripwire) and WI-11 into five beads (spawn/done, compact/checkpoint, planning-promotion, Fly D14 block, roles refs+lint).
autoDecisions.rationale: Each is an independently reviewable, independently testable change touching distinct files; the aggressive-decomposition rule prefers many small beads, and the constant split is a genuine cross-cutting foundation the guards depend on.

autoDecisions.summary: Marked exactly three beads requiresInspection:true (STATE_BRANCH_PATHS constant, resolveStateHome, migrate-command) at inspectionDepth:deep.
autoDecisions.rationale: These are the plan's true foundations: the constant is consumed by four downstream beads; resolveStateHome is the resolution chokepoint every door depends on; the migration is the one-time data cutover on main. Every other bead's defects surface immediately at typecheck/lint/its named test.

autoDecisions.summary: Classified nearly all beads readiness:sequential rather than ready.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD's execution mode is a single operator-supervised agent working directly on main (not the parallel swarm), and the beads have real ordering dependencies (foundation -> doors -> migration -> remediation). Sequential is the honest classification and avoids false parallel-safety claims.

Keep the existing diff-classification predicate that retains workspace-local .pan/continue.json as ignore-this-diff runtime state, distinct from branch content, so nothing hand-copies a path list.

Extend resolveInfraRepo in src/lib/projects.ts:353 so migrated projects resolve to the state worktree with recordsPath '.'; add a doctor self-heal hook that repairs a missing/dirty/wrong-branch worktree.

Add idempotent pan admin state migrate <project> cutover command

expected_outputs: typecheck completes with no errors
integration test asserts the migrated tree matches D2, main carries no state paths, and re-run is a no-op

narrative.Action: Implement pan admin state migrate <project> as a single idempotent command: create the orphan branch overdeck-state seeded from main's tracked tree via a temp index (git read-tree/commit-tree, no primary-worktree checkout gymnastics) applying the WI-2 path mapping (.pan/records -> records, ... , .beads -> .beads, .pan/context NOT migrated); copy the verified untracked stray .pan-root files into notes/ and commit them; push the branch and create the state worktree; then in one ordinary commit on main git rm -r --cached the migrated paths, git mv .pan/context .overdeck/context, and rewrite the state-path .gitignore entries. Provide a --dry-run plan and require a throwaway-clone checkpoint before any write; recovery from failure is git revert on main plus branch deletion.

items.title: After running on a fixture repo, git ls-tree overdeck-state contains records/, continues/, specs/, drafts/, review/, test/, feedback/, backlog/, notes/, and .beads/ at its root and no .pan/ wrapper.
After migration git ls-tree main contains no .pan/ path and no .beads/ path, and .pan/context has moved to .overdeck/context.
Re-running the command on an already-migrated project exits 0 and prints 'already migrated' without creating a second commit.
The command commits the verified untracked stray .pan-root files into notes/ and removes them from the primary checkout.
Under --dry-run the command prints a full plan and makes no writes, and otherwise commits only ordinary revertible commits with no history rewrite on main.

Audit the remaining direct .pan/ references and route state reads through the doors; workspace-local runtime references stay in the context-runtime-rename bead's scope, not this one.

Each read door (records, continue, drafts, feedback, backlog sequence) resolves its base directory through resolveStateHome, verified by a per-domain unit test.
Harden the write door to commit only in the state worktree on overdeck-state

expected_outputs: typecheck completes with no errors
auto-commit.test.ts asserts state commits land on overdeck-state, branch-assertion blocks a bad commit, and the fake-timer retry loop runs

narrative.Action: Harden queueAutoCommit (line 189) and flushAutoCommits (line 241) in src/lib/pan-dir/auto-commit.ts so state-path commits route to the state worktree only, assert git branch --show-current equals overdeck-state before every commit, and push after flush with the D10 fetch/rebase/retry loop (bounded 3 attempts, re-reading the canonical value through the read door on conflict). When the worktree is missing, refuse the write with a log and surface rather than discarding it. Per NFR-3, every retry/delay test uses vi.useFakeTimers() and vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(), never real timers.

items.title: A queued state write on a migrated project produces a commit on overdeck-state inside the state worktree and never on main.
The write door asserts the current branch is overdeck-state and blocks the commit when the assertion fails.
The bounded rebase-retry loop applies the queued write after re-reading the canonical value, exercised with vi.useFakeTimers() and no real waits.
When the state worktree is missing, the write door refuses the commit, logs the failure, and surfaces it rather than discarding the write.
Relocate beads to the state worktree via redirect retarget and -C flag

expected_outputs: typecheck completes with no errors

narrative.Action: Per D13, retarget the gitignored .beads/redirect that initializeWorkspaceBeads writes: on a migrated project it records the state worktree's absolute .beads path (from resolveStateHome) and its existsSync precondition checks the state worktree; unmigrated projects keep writing ../../.beads gated on isStateMigrated(). Add -C <state worktree> to project-scope bd invocations, target queueBeadsAutoCommit (auto-commit.ts:227) at the state worktree, and key the 422 beads-missing gate off the redirect/shared DB rather than a committed workspace issues.jsonl.

items.title: initializeWorkspaceBeads records the redirect target as the state worktree's absolute .beads path on a migrated project and falls back to ../../.beads on an unmigrated project.
Project-scope bd command construction contains -C <state worktree>, so bd ready resolves the state worktree's .beads database.
The 422 beads-missing gate still blocks agent start when no beads exist for the issue, now keyed off the shared DB via the redirect, and existing workspace beads tests stay green.

Add branch filters in .github/workflows/*.yml so overdeck-state pushes run only the state-tree guard and no other workflow (NFR-2).
